question: Following tip-offs, the Commission has suspended payments for projects with links to the controversial political scientist Farid Hafez and the ‘I Report’ project, meaning that the European Union logo has disappeared from related reports.
However, there is growing evidence that other organisations with links to the Muslim Brotherhood are trying to get EU funding through the CLAIM Alliance, which also launched the ‘I Report’ project.

CLAIM Alliance organisations that have been linked to the Muslim Brotherhood include the Muslim Youths in Germany (MJD), the Muslim Centre for Girls, Women and Family (RAHMA), the Council of Muslim Students and Academics (RAMSA), and the Meeting and Training Centre of Muslim Women (BFmF). 1.
Has the Commission given money to the CLAIM Alliance or any of its affiliated organisations?
Is the Commission aware that Farid Hafez has once again tried to obtain EU funds through the CLAIM Alliance?
What measures is the Commission taking to verify applications for EU funds made by organisations or individuals that may have links to the Muslim Brotherhood?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.7.2024) The Honourable Member is referred to the Financial Transparency System1 publishing the recipients of EU funds under direct and indirect management. Under shared management, the organisation ‘Ufuq.

de’, member of the CLAIM Alliance on the CLAIM Alliance website2, was a co-beneficiary in a de-radicalisation project under the German Internal Security Fund Programme 2014-2020. The Commission did not identify other recent instances where EU funding would have been allocated to organisations that are members of the CLAIM Alliance or their participation in any recent calls for proposals for EU funds.

Under the Financial Regulation3, the Commission can launch a procedure on early-detection and exclusion system4 (EDES) to protect the EU budget and exclude entities from award procedures. The Commission verifies the respect of EU values during the selection and evaluation process (EDES, declarations on honour or, where applicable, eligibility criteria related to EU values), and can reject applicants.

The Financial Regulation recast (expected to apply from October 2024) will further protect EU values by introducing a specific EDES exclusion ground based on the incitement to discrimination, hatred or violence or similar activities contrary to the EU values under Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union5, which negatively affects or concretely risks affecting the performance of a legal commitment.
